name: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
description: When users hit a problem, the interface should explain it in plain language and make the path to recovery obvious. The goal is not merely surfacing an error state, but helping people understand what went wrong and recover without getting stuck.
design_relevance_note: Applies to form validation, payment failures, permission problems, upload errors, broken states after sync conflicts, and any recovery UI that needs to turn confusion into an actionable next step.
myth_risk_note: Existing corpus backing supports error-recovery documentation specifically but not a comprehensive interface-design principle. This pass added no new HCI evidence. The heuristic remains incompletely validated for general interface design, consistent with the existing partial status.
prevalence_note: A standard item in heuristic reviews and UX writing, especially for forms, onboarding, and transactional flows, though the full Nielsen phrasing is used more in usability practice than in day-to-day product slang.

findings.description: A controlled experiment over several semesters in a CS1 course found enhancing compiler error message clarity produced NO measurable reduction in consecutive same-error submissions -- despite anecdotal reports, student surveys, and instructor opinions all testifying to the enhancement's perceived helpfulness. The authors explicitly note their result contradicts one prior study while validating another, characterizing the field's findings on this question as genuinely mixed.
findings.source_title: Do Enhanced Compiler Error Messages Help Students?

findings.description: A controlled intervention study enhancing Java compiler error messages found the intervention group had fewer overall errors, fewer errors per student, and fewer repeated-error occurrences than the control group -- direct evidence that clarifying error messages can measurably improve novice programmers' error-recovery outcomes, in the narrower domain of programming/compiler errors rather than general end-user UI errors.
findings.source_title: Effective compiler error message enhancement for novice programming students

findings.description: Two controlled experiments comparing a deliberately brief, error-recovery-focused 'Minimal Manual' against an otherwise comparable commercial self-instruction manual found the minimal version produced more efficient learning progress, specifically in the areas its design predicted. Supports the underlying premise behind the 'paradox of the active user': people learning new software tend to start doing rather than read comprehensive instructions first, so documentation built around that behavior (short, task-focused, strong on error recovery) outperforms documentation that assumes people will read it start to finish.

applications.title: Amazon combines border highlighting, iconography, and red text to make form errors hard to miss
applications.description: Nielsen Norman Group's error-message guidelines article names Amazon as a positive example of the visibility guideline for Nielsen's 9th usability heuristic ('help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors'): the site layers several redundant, accessible signals -- a highlighted field border, an icon, and red text -- rather than relying on a single subtle cue, so users with varying attention or color perception are still likely to notice and locate the error.
applications.ethical_note: Redundant, accessible error signaling that helps users of varying ability notice and fix mistakes; no persuasive or manipulative dimension.

applications.title: Disneyworld's dining search used puns instead of a clear message when narrow filters returned no results
applications.description: Nielsen Norman Group's error-message guidelines article names Disneyworld's dining-location search as a negative example of the communication guideline for Nielsen's 9th usability heuristic: when a user's narrow filter combination returned no matching restaurants, the site's response leaned on wordplay/puns rather than concisely and precisely stating that no results matched and suggesting how to adjust the filters -- leaving users unclear on what actually happened or what to do next.
applications.ethical_note: A clarity shortcoming: users are left confused about why no results appeared and unsure how to adjust their search filters to get a useful result, not a persuasive or manipulative pattern.
